extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (schools, colleges, universities), Title IX coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, institutional legal counsel, and policymakers implementing §106.45
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for recipients on how to implement and comply with the Department of Education's final §106.45 grievance process for Title IX sexual harassment complaints, including required procedures, limits, training, and enforcement expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement without regard to protected characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will enforce all provisions of §106.45 without regard to any party's sex, race, ethnicity, or other characteristic, and expects recipients to implement §106.45 without bias of any kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must apply §106.45 neutrally; enforcement is not to be influenced by any party's protected characteristics. The Department will enforce compliance irrespective of a recipient's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt, non-deliberately indifferent response and supportive measures (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(a) obligates a recipient to provide a prompt, non-deliberately indifferent response to each complainant including offering supportive measures, whether or not the complainant files a formal complaint or participates in a §106.45 grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must offer supportive measures to complainants even if they do not file a formal complaint or participate in the grievance process; supportive measures are separate from the §106.45 formal grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisor status and parties' financial resources must not affect compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The status of any party's advisor (i.e., whether a party's advisor is an attorney or not), the financial resources of any party, and the potential of any party to yield financial benefits to a recipient, must not affect the recipient's compliance with §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients cannot give advantage or disadvantage based on whether a party can afford an advisor; must objectively evaluate evidence and use unbiased investigators and decision-makers regardless of advisor status or party resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must not discharge Title IX obligations by referring to law enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient cannot discharge its legal obligation to provide education programs or activities free from sex discrimination by referring Title IX sexual harassment allegations to law enforcement (or requiring or advising complainants to do so).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where allegations may also be criminal, recipients must independently respond under Title IX to provide remedies and supportive measures; nothing prohibits a complainant from pursuing criminal charges in addition to a §106.45 process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to adjudicate formal complaints under §106.45 to provide remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department is requiring recipients to adjudicate allegations that sex-based conduct has deprived a complainant of equal access to education and remedy such situations to further Title IX's non-discrimination mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The §106.45 grievance process is designed to reliably determine facts so recipients can provide appropriate remedies when a respondent is found responsible; this is distinct from criminal adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process founded on reliable fact-finding principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedures required under §106.45 are those the Department has determined are most likely to lead to reliable outcomes in the context of Title IX sexual harassment; the process effectuates Title IX by promoting reliable fact-finding and reducing sex-based bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures emphasize objective evaluation of relevant evidence, impartial investigators/decision-makers, training to avoid prejudgment and stereotypes, and standardized steps to increase consistency and reliability across recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may facilitate informal resolution but cannot require mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: While the final regulations permit recipients wide discretion to facilitate informal resolution of formal complaints of sexual harassment, the Department declines to require parties to attempt mediation before initiating the formal grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision to attempt mediation or other informal resolution should remain with each party; recipients can offer but not mandate informal resolutions as an alternative to the formal §106.45 process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of regional centers and outsourcing (voluntary, not mandated)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department encourages recipients to consider innovative models (e.g., regional centers, consortia, state agencies, independent 501(c)(3) organizations) to outsource or cooperatively handle investigation and adjudication, but does not mandate such models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may form or join voluntary cooperative models to obtain trained, impartial investigators/decision-makers and reduce inherent conflicts of interest; the Department will provide technical assistance on such options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: §106.45 applies to all Title IX sexual harassment categories (§106.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45 applies to formal complaints alleging any type of sexual harassment as defined in §106.30 (quid pro quo by an employee; severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive conduct; sexual assault/dating violence/domestic violence/stalking as defined under Clery Act and VAWA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to limit §106.45 only to sexual assault or to complaints where respondent faces expulsion; all categories of defined sexual harassment must be handled under a process designed to reliably determine facts and provide remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the term 'grievance process that complies with §106.45' instead of 'due process'
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid confusion between constitutional due process and a fair process required of all recipients, the final regulations use the phrase 'grievance process that complies with §106.45' instead of 'due process' or 'due process protections.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that the §106.45 grievance process draws from due process principles but is distinct from constitutional due process (which applies only to state actors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of all relevant evidence; no prejudgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have an obligation to objectively evaluate relevant evidence and to use investigators and decision-makers free from bias or conflicts of interest; §106.45 aims to avoid prejudgment of the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators and decision-makers must evaluate evidence impartially, avoid sex-based stereotypes, and not make credibility determinations based solely on party status (complainant/respondent). Either party may appeal on the ground that bias or conflict affected the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirement for Title IX personnel on impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(iii) requires Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and individuals who facilitate any informal resolution process to be free of bias or conflicts of interest and to be trained on how to serve impartially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must address avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, sex-based biases and stereotypes, and procedures for impartial fact-finding; recipients should ensure personnel receive such training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that respondent is not responsible until conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(iv) requires recipients to presume the respondent is not responsible until conclusion of the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption reinforces that the burden of proof remains on the recipient and supports correct application of the selected standard of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rape-shield protections for complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(6)(i)-(ii) protects complainants (but not respondents) from questions or evidence about the complainant's prior sexual behavior or sexual predisposition, mirroring rape-shield protections applied in Federal courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These limits are an exception to otherwise generally equal treatment of parties and are justified to reasonably promote truth-seeking in sexual harassment proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on credibility determinations based solely on party status
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(ii) precludes credibility determinations based on a person's status as a complainant, respondent, or witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-makers must evaluate credibility based on evidence and testimony, not on the role a person plays in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal rights and opportunities to participate; limited exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The §106.45 grievance process aims to provide both parties equal rights and opportunities to participate in the process, with three specified exceptions (equitable remedies for complainants, presumption of non-responsibility for respondents, and rape-shield protections for complainants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly all provisions apply equally to complainants and respondents; where differences exist they are party-status specific to promote truth-seeking and equitable outcomes, not to discriminate based on sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' discretion on sanctions and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not prescribe any particular form of disciplinary sanction for sexual harassment; recipients maintain discretion to impose sanctions after following §106.45 procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must follow the grievance process for fact-finding before imposing discipline, but may choose appropriate sanctions consistent with institutional policies and applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement expectations and corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will enforce §106.45 regardless of a recipient's intent to violate the rule; corrective action required after identified violations depends on the facts of each enforcement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department typically notifies recipients and seeks correction before imposing severe remedies; the Department will not require parties to preserve objections because compliance obligations exist independently of party objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal based on bias or conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party may file an appeal on the ground that the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decision-maker had a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally, or the individual party, that affected the outcome of the matter (see §106.45(b)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals provide a mechanism to address alleged impartiality failures; recipients should ensure appellate processes can consider and remedy such issues where they affected outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal of preventing injection of sex-based stereotypes and discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The §106.45 grievance process is designed to avoid injection of sex-based biases and stereotypes into Title IX proceedings and to promote reliable outcomes that protect individuals from discriminatory practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural protections (training, objective evidence evaluation, rape-shield rules, presumption of non-responsibility, etc.) are intended to reduce opportunities for sex discrimination and increase perceived and actual fairness.
